chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from al-Qasim ibn 'Urwah, from Ibn Bukayr, from Zurarah, from Abi 'Abd Allah عليه السلام: concerning

A man who forgets to wipe his head until he enters into the salat (prayer) — he said: “If there is moisture in his beard equal to what he can wipe his head and his feet with, then let him do that and let him pray.” He said: “And if he forgets something from the obligatory wudu (ablution), then he must begin with what he forgot and repeat what remains so that the wudu (ablution) may be completed.”

Al-Shaykh, may Allah the Exalted support him, said: Whoever is sitting in the state of performing wudu (ablution) and has not yet finished it, then a supposition occurs to him that he may have done something that nullifies his wudu (ablution), or he imagines that he advanced what should be delayed in it or delayed what should be advanced, then it is obligatory upon him to repeat the wudu (ablution) from its beginning, so that he may rise from his sitting-place having completed his wudu (ablution) with certainty, safe from invalidity. But if doubt occurs to him about it after finishing it and after rising from his place, he should pay no attention to that and should rule on the basis of certainty. And if he becomes certain that it has indeed been invalidated by an occurrence that corrupts taharah (ritual purity), or by advancing what should be delayed or delaying what should be advanced, he must repeat the wudu (ablution) from its beginning. This is indicated by that.

key_terms.الْمَفْرُوضِ: the obligatory part required by law
key_terms.شَكٌّ: doubt occurring regarding the validity or order of wudu (ablution)
key_terms.لِحْيَتِهِ: his beard, whose moisture may be used for wiping
key_terms.يَقِينٍ: certainty upon which one bases action

ai.seo_question: What should a person do if he forgets part of wudu (ablution) or doubts it during or after completing it?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses rulings related to wudu (ablution), especially when part of it is forgotten or when doubt arises during or after its performance. It distinguishes between doubt before completion, which requires restarting for certainty, and doubt after completion, which is ignored unless one becomes certain that the wudu (ablution) was invalidated.
